description: Manage an IT change from request through implementation and verification.

steps.description: Submit a change request with impact and risk assessment.

inputs.name: change-description
inputs.desc: What is being changed and why

inputs.name: affected-systems
inputs.desc: Systems and services affected by the change

outputs.name: change-request
outputs.desc: Completed change request form

outputs.name: impact-assessment
outputs.desc: Impact and risk rating for the change

process: Describe the change, its purpose, and the expected outcome.
Identify all affected systems, services, and users.
Assess the risk (likelihood of failure times severity of impact).
Document the rollback procedure.

steps.description: Classify the change as standard, normal, or emergency.

outputs.name: change-classification
outputs.desc: Classification: standard, normal, or emergency

outputs.name: approval-requirements
outputs.desc: Who must approve based on classification

process: Compare the change against pre-approved standard change models.
If no standard model matches, classify as normal or emergency based on urgency.
Determine the approval path for the classification.
Assign the change to the appropriate review queue.

steps.description: Review and approve the change through the advisory board.

outputs.name: approval-decision
outputs.desc: Approved, rejected, or deferred with rationale

outputs.name: conditions
outputs.desc: Any conditions attached to the approval

process: Present the change to the advisory board with the impact assessment.
Review the rollback plan and test evidence.
Vote on approval, rejection, or deferral.
Record the decision and any conditions.

steps.description: Schedule the change implementation window.

outputs.name: change-schedule
outputs.desc: Scheduled date, time, and duration

outputs.name: notification-plan
outputs.desc: Who to notify before, during, and after

process: Check the change calendar for conflicts.
Select a window that minimizes user impact.
Notify all stakeholders of the scheduled window.
Confirm resource availability for the window.

steps.description: Implement the change and verify success.

inputs.name: change-request
inputs.desc: The change request with implementation steps

outputs.name: implementation-result
outputs.desc: Success or failure with details

outputs.name: change-record
outputs.desc: Final change record with timeline and outcome

process: Execute the change steps per the implementation plan.
Run verification tests after each step.
If any step fails, execute the rollback procedure.
Document the outcome in the change record and close.

description: Manage an IT asset from procurement through secure disposal.

steps.description: Procure and receive an IT asset.

inputs.name: asset-request
inputs.desc: What asset is needed and the business justification

outputs.name: purchase-order
outputs.desc: Issued purchase order

outputs.name: receiving-record
outputs.desc: Record of asset receipt and inspection

process: Issue the purchase order to the selected vendor.
Receive and inspect the asset against the order.
Record the serial number, model, and condition.
Store the asset until deployment.

steps.description: Register the asset in the inventory and CMDB.

outputs.name: asset-record
outputs.desc: CMDB record for the asset

outputs.name: asset-tag
outputs.desc: Assigned asset tag and barcode

process: Create the asset record in the CMDB with all hardware and software details.
Assign the asset tag and affix the barcode label.
Record the purchase cost, warranty terms, and vendor contact.
Link the asset to its configuration items.

steps.description: Deploy the asset to the assigned user.

outputs.name: deployment-record
outputs.desc: Record of who received the asset, when, and where

outputs.name: user-acknowledgment
outputs.desc: User sign-off on receipt and acceptable use

process: Image or configure the asset per the standard build.
Deliver to the user and verify functionality.
Collect the user acknowledgment of receipt and policy.
Update the CMDB with the assigned user and location.

steps.description: Track asset usage, warranty, and maintenance needs.

outputs.name: usage-report
outputs.desc: Asset utilization and health data

outputs.name: refresh-recommendation
outputs.desc: Whether the asset should be refreshed or retired

process: Monitor utilization metrics (CPU, disk, age, repair history).
Track warranty status and upcoming expirations.
Flag assets that exceed the refresh threshold.
Produce the usage report with refresh recommendations.

steps.description: Securely dispose of or recycle a retired asset.

outputs.name: disposal-certificate
outputs.desc: Certificate of secure data destruction

outputs.name: lifecycle-report
outputs.desc: Complete lifecycle report from procurement to disposal

process: Remove all data using certified wiping or physical destruction.
Obtain the certificate of destruction from the disposal vendor.
Update the CMDB to mark the asset as disposed.
Archive the complete lifecycle record.

description: Design and publish an IT service catalog.

steps.description: Inventory all IT services currently provided.

inputs.name: existing-documentation
inputs.desc: Any existing service lists or documentation

outputs.name: service-inventory
outputs.desc: List of all IT services with owners

outputs.name: service-gaps
outputs.desc: Services that are provided but undocumented

process: Interview each IT team to identify the services they provide.
Cross-reference with ticket categories and request types.
Identify services that are provided but not formally documented.
Compile the complete service inventory.

steps.description: Categorize services by business function.

outputs.name: service-categories
outputs.desc: Services grouped by business function

outputs.name: category-hierarchy
outputs.desc: The category tree structure

process: Group services by the business function they support (communication, productivity, security, infrastructure).
Define the hierarchy of categories and subcategories.
Assign each service to exactly one primary category.
Review with business stakeholders for alignment.

steps.description: Write the service definition for each catalog entry.

outputs.name: service-definitions
outputs.desc: Complete definition for each service (description, SLA, cost, owner)

outputs.name: sla-matrix
outputs.desc: SLA targets for each service

process: Write the description, scope, and eligibility for each service.
Define the SLA targets (availability, response time, resolution time).
Assign the service owner and support team.
Document the cost model if applicable.

steps.description: Build the request fulfillment workflows for each service.

inputs.name: service-definitions
inputs.desc: Service definitions with scope and SLA

outputs.name: request-workflows
outputs.desc: Fulfillment workflows for each requestable service

outputs.name: approval-matrix
outputs.desc: Who approves each type of request

process: Map the fulfillment steps for each requestable service.
Define the approval requirements by cost and risk.
Build the request forms with required fields.
Test each workflow end to end.

steps.description: Publish the catalog and establish the review cadence.

outputs.name: published-catalog
outputs.desc: The published service catalog

outputs.name: review-schedule
outputs.desc: Quarterly review and update schedule

process: Assemble all definitions, categories, and workflows into the catalog format.
Publish to the self-service portal.
Announce the catalog to all users with instructions.
Schedule the first quarterly review.

description: Investigate and permanently resolve the root cause of recurring incidents.

steps.description: Identify recurring incidents that indicate an underlying problem.

inputs.name: incident-data
inputs.desc: Incident records from the service desk

inputs.name: threshold-criteria
inputs.desc: How many recurrences qualify as a problem

outputs.name: problem-candidates
outputs.desc: Incidents that recur above the threshold

outputs.name: pattern-analysis
outputs.desc: Commonalities across the recurring incidents

process: Query incident records for clusters by category, CI, or symptom.
Identify patterns that exceed the recurrence threshold.
Group related incidents into candidate problems.
Rank by business impact and frequency.

steps.description: Open a formal problem record and assign ownership.

outputs.name: problem-record
outputs.desc: Formal problem record with assigned owner

outputs.name: investigation-scope
outputs.desc: Scope and timeline for the investigation

process: Select the highest-priority candidate.
Create the problem record with all linked incidents.
Assign the problem owner and investigation team.
Define the investigation scope and deadline.

steps.description: Investigate the root cause of the problem.

inputs.name: investigation-scope
inputs.desc: What to investigate and by when

outputs.name: root-cause
outputs.desc: Identified root cause with evidence

outputs.name: workaround
outputs.desc: Interim workaround if available

process: Collect logs, metrics, and configuration data from the affected systems.
Apply root cause analysis techniques (5 Why, fault tree, timeline analysis).
Identify and document the root cause with supporting evidence.
Define an interim workaround if the permanent fix will take time.

steps.description: Develop, test, and implement the permanent fix.

outputs.name: fix-implementation
outputs.desc: The implemented permanent fix

outputs.name: test-evidence
outputs.desc: Evidence that the fix resolves the problem

process: Design the permanent fix that addresses the root cause.
Test the fix in a non-production environment.
Submit the fix through the change management process.
Implement and verify in production.

steps.description: Update the known error database and close the problem.

outputs.name: known-error-entry
outputs.desc: Entry in the known error database

outputs.name: closed-problem-record
outputs.desc: Closed problem record with full documentation

process: Create or update the known error database entry.
Link the root cause, workaround, and permanent fix.
Close all linked incidents.
Close the problem record.

description: Set up configuration management with a CMDB for tracking configuration items and their relationships.

steps.description: Define the scope and depth of the CMDB.

inputs.name: it-environment
inputs.desc: Overview of the IT environment (servers, network, applications)

inputs.name: business-priorities
inputs.desc: Which services and systems matter most

outputs.name: cmdb-scope
outputs.desc: What configuration items to track and at what depth

outputs.name: ci-types
outputs.desc: The types of configuration items and their attributes

process: Identify the CI types to track (hardware, software, network, cloud, services).
Define the attributes to capture for each CI type.
Set the depth: track to the server level, component level, or both.
Prioritize: start with CIs that support critical business services.

steps.description: Map the relationships between configuration items.

outputs.name: relationship-model
outputs.desc: How CIs relate to each other (depends on, runs on, connects to)

outputs.name: service-maps
outputs.desc: Service dependency maps for critical services

process: Define the relationship types (depends on, runs on, connects to, contains).
Map the dependencies for each critical service top-down.
Validate the maps by walking a recent incident's impact path.
Document the relationship model.

steps.description: Set up automated discovery and reconciliation.

outputs.name: discovery-configuration
outputs.desc: Configured discovery tool settings

outputs.name: reconciliation-rules
outputs.desc: Rules for matching discovered CIs to existing records

process: Select and configure the discovery tool for each CI type.
Define the reconciliation rules (match on serial number, hostname, MAC).
Run the initial discovery scan and review the results.
Resolve any duplicates or mismatches.

steps.description: Track changes to configuration items over time.

outputs.name: change-tracking-policy
outputs.desc: How unauthorized changes are detected and flagged

outputs.name: baseline-snapshots
outputs.desc: Baseline snapshots for each CI type

process: Capture the baseline state of all CIs.
Schedule regular discovery scans to detect drift.
Flag unauthorized changes for investigation.
Integrate with the change management process so approved changes update the CMDB.

steps.description: Schedule and run CMDB accuracy audits.

outputs.name: audit-schedule
outputs.desc: Recurring audit schedule by CI type

outputs.name: cmdb-management-plan
outputs.desc: Complete CMDB management plan with roles, processes, and metrics

process: Define the audit frequency by CI type and criticality.
Sample CIs and verify against physical reality.
Measure CMDB accuracy (percentage of CIs that match reality).
Document the complete CMDB management plan.

description: Fulfill IT service requests from receipt through closure.

steps.description: Receive and validate the service request.

inputs.name: requester-info
inputs.desc: Who is making the request and their role

outputs.name: validated-request
outputs.desc: Request validated against the service catalog

outputs.name: fulfillment-path
outputs.desc: Which team and workflow will fulfill this request

process: Match the request to a service catalog entry.
Verify the requester is eligible for the service.
Check if approval is required based on the approval matrix.
Route to the appropriate fulfillment team.

steps.description: Route the request through the approval chain if required.

outputs.name: approved-request
outputs.desc: Approved request ready for fulfillment

outputs.name: approval-record
outputs.desc: Record of who approved and when

process: Determine if the request requires approval.
If yes, send to the approver with the request details and cost.
Track the approval timeline against the SLA.
Record the approval or rejection.

steps.description: Execute the provisioning steps to fulfill the request.

outputs.name: provisioning-result
outputs.desc: What was provisioned and its status

outputs.name: delivery-details
outputs.desc: How and when the user can access the fulfilled request

process: Execute each provisioning step per the fulfillment workflow.
Configure access, licenses, or hardware as specified.
Test the provisioned service or asset.
Prepare the delivery notification for the requester.

steps.description: Verify fulfillment with the requester and close.

outputs.name: user-confirmation
outputs.desc: User confirmation that the request is fulfilled

outputs.name: fulfillment-record
outputs.desc: Complete fulfillment record with timeline and satisfaction

process: Notify the requester that the service is ready.
Confirm the requester can access and use the service.
Collect satisfaction feedback.
Close the request and archive the fulfillment record.

description: Plan IT service continuity to maintain critical services during a disruption.

steps.description: Identify critical IT services and their dependencies.

inputs.name: service-catalog
inputs.desc: IT service catalog or service list

inputs.name: business-impact-data
inputs.desc: Business impact if each service is unavailable

outputs.name: critical-services
outputs.desc: Ranked list of critical services

outputs.name: dependency-map
outputs.desc: Dependencies for each critical service

process: Rank services by business impact of downtime.
Identify the top tier of services that must be recovered first.
Map the infrastructure, application, and data dependencies for each.
Identify single points of failure.

steps.description: Define recovery time and recovery point objectives.

outputs.name: recovery-objectives
outputs.desc: RTO and RPO for each critical service

outputs.name: recovery-tiers
outputs.desc: Services grouped by recovery priority tier

process: Set the RTO (maximum acceptable downtime) for each service.
Set the RPO (maximum acceptable data loss) for each service.
Group services into recovery tiers by priority.
Validate objectives are achievable with current infrastructure.

steps.description: Design the recovery procedures for each critical service.

outputs.name: recovery-procedures
outputs.desc: Step-by-step recovery procedures per service

outputs.name: resource-requirements
outputs.desc: People, infrastructure, and data needed for recovery

process: Design the recovery steps for each service in dependency order.
Identify the personnel, infrastructure, and data backups required.
Document the communication plan during recovery.
Define the criteria for declaring the service recovered.

steps.description: Test the continuity plan with a tabletop or simulation exercise.

outputs.name: test-results
outputs.desc: Results of the continuity test including gaps found

outputs.name: continuity-plan
outputs.desc: Final IT service continuity plan incorporating test findings

process: Design the test scenario (tabletop walkthrough or live simulation).
Execute the test with the recovery team.
Measure actual recovery times against RTO and RPO targets.
Document gaps and update the continuity plan.

description: Manage a major IT incident from declaration through post-incident review.

steps.description: Declare a major incident and activate the response.

inputs.name: incident-report
inputs.desc: The incident that triggered the major incident declaration

inputs.name: impact-scope
inputs.desc: Number of users, services, and business functions affected

outputs.name: major-incident-record
outputs.desc: Formal major incident record with severity and scope

outputs.name: response-activation
outputs.desc: Response team and communication bridge details

process: Assess whether the incident meets major incident criteria.
Declare the major incident and assign a severity level.
Activate the major incident response team.
Open the communication bridge (war room or call).

steps.description: Diagnose the issue and restore the affected service.

outputs.name: diagnosis
outputs.desc: What went wrong and what was done to restore

outputs.name: restoration-confirmation
outputs.desc: Confirmation that the service is restored

process: Gather symptoms, logs, and metrics to identify the failure.
Identify and implement the fastest path to restore the service.
Verify the service is functioning for all affected users.
Document the timeline of actions taken.

steps.description: Communicate status to stakeholders throughout the incident.

outputs.name: communication-log
outputs.desc: All communications sent during the incident

outputs.name: stakeholder-updates
outputs.desc: Status updates sent to business stakeholders

process: Send the initial notification to all stakeholders.
Provide regular updates at the defined cadence (every 30 minutes).
Send the resolution notification when the service is restored.
Record all communications in the incident log.

steps.description: Conduct the post-incident review and produce the report.

outputs.name: post-incident-report
outputs.desc: Blameless post-incident report with timeline and root cause

outputs.name: improvement-actions
outputs.desc: Action items to prevent recurrence

process: Assemble the timeline from detection to resolution.
Identify the root cause and contributing factors.
Define action items to prevent recurrence.
Publish the blameless post-incident report.

description: Define, monitor, and manage IT service level agreements.

steps.description: Define SLAs for IT services.

inputs.name: service-catalog
inputs.desc: IT service catalog with service definitions

outputs.name: sla-drafts
outputs.desc: Draft SLAs for each service

outputs.name: measurement-criteria
outputs.desc: How each SLA metric will be measured

process: Identify the SLA metrics for each service (availability, response time, resolution time).
Set the target levels based on business requirements.
Define how each metric will be measured and reported.
Draft the SLA document for each service.

steps.description: Negotiate SLA terms with business stakeholders.

outputs.name: agreed-slas
outputs.desc: SLAs agreed upon by IT and business stakeholders

outputs.name: escalation-procedures
outputs.desc: What happens when an SLA is breached

process: Present the draft SLAs to business stakeholders.
Negotiate targets that are achievable and meet business needs.
Define the escalation procedures for SLA breaches.
Sign off on the agreed SLAs.

steps.description: Monitor SLA performance and produce reports.

outputs.name: performance-reports
outputs.desc: Regular SLA performance reports

outputs.name: breach-alerts
outputs.desc: Alerts when SLA thresholds are at risk or breached

process: Set up automated monitoring for each SLA metric.
Generate regular performance reports (weekly, monthly).
Alert the service owner when a metric approaches or breaches the target.
Track trends over time to identify degradation.

steps.description: Review SLA performance annually and renegotiate terms.

outputs.name: updated-slas
outputs.desc: Updated SLAs for the next period

outputs.name: sla-management-document
outputs.desc: Complete SLA management document with history and current terms

process: Review the past year's SLA performance.
Identify SLAs that were consistently met, missed, or irrelevant.
Propose adjustments based on changing business needs.
Agree on updated terms and publish the SLA management document.

description: Plan and manage IT infrastructure capacity to meet current and future demand.

steps.description: Collect utilization data for compute, storage, and network.

inputs.name: infrastructure-scope
inputs.desc: Which infrastructure to monitor (servers, storage, network, cloud)

inputs.name: monitoring-tools
inputs.desc: Available monitoring tools and data sources

outputs.name: utilization-data
outputs.desc: Current utilization metrics for all infrastructure components

outputs.name: utilization-baselines
outputs.desc: Baseline utilization levels for normal and peak periods

process: Connect to monitoring tools and collect CPU, memory, disk, and network metrics.
Establish baseline utilization for normal business hours and peak periods.
Identify components that are consistently above 80% utilization.
Flag components with no monitoring coverage.

steps.description: Forecast future capacity demand based on business plans.

outputs.name: demand-forecast
outputs.desc: Projected capacity needs for the next 12 months

outputs.name: growth-assumptions
outputs.desc: Business growth assumptions used in the forecast

process: Collect business growth plans (new users, applications, regions).
Model the capacity impact of each growth driver.
Project utilization forward at 3, 6, and 12 month intervals.
Document the assumptions behind each projection.

steps.description: Identify capacity shortfalls and over-provisioned resources.

outputs.name: capacity-gaps
outputs.desc: Components that will exceed capacity within the forecast period

outputs.name: optimization-opportunities
outputs.desc: Over-provisioned resources that can be right-sized

process: Compare the demand forecast against current capacity.
Identify components that will hit capacity limits.
Identify components that are over-provisioned and can be downsized.
Rank gaps by business impact and urgency.

steps.description: Plan and implement the capacity changes.

outputs.name: capacity-actions
outputs.desc: Planned procurement, scaling, or optimization actions

outputs.name: capacity-management-report
outputs.desc: Complete capacity management report with current state, forecast, and actions

process: Define the action for each gap (procure, scale, optimize, migrate).
Estimate the cost and timeline for each action.
Submit procurement or change requests as needed.
Document the complete capacity management report.
